short: The second and so far last use of a nuclear weapon in war, three days after Hiroshima.
full:
Nagasaki was the secondary target on 9 August 1945. Cloud covered the primary, the arsenal city of Kokura, and the B-29 Bockscar turned away with fuel running short. The plutonium implosion bomb, Fat Man, detonated at 11.02am about 500 metres above the Urakami valley, well north of the intended aiming point. The surrounding hills confined the blast: the yield was around 21 kilotons, greater than Hiroshima's, but the death toll was lower. Between 39,000 and 80,000 people died by the end of 1945, roughly half of them on the first day.

The Soviet Union had declared war on Japan and invaded Manchuria hours earlier. Japan's leadership, deadlocked between surrender and a final defensive battle in the home islands, was broken by the combination, and the Emperor intervened to accept the Allied terms. No nuclear weapon has been used in war since. Argument over whether these two were necessary, or whether the Soviet entry alone would have sufficed, has continued for eighty years.
